title: When are optimal transport maps stable?
question: For a uniform square source and targets with exactly three atoms in that square, does a fixed positive lower bound on every atom’s mass imply a uniform square-root stability bound, without separation or angle assumptions?
summary: A recent three-atom example produces cube-root instability by letting one target mass vanish. Determine whether a positive mass floor restores square-root stability: reproduce the example with independent mass and displacement, prove a separated-site estimate, then remove separation or give a counterexample.
